symptoms: Uniform dark green foliage without chlorosis
Turgid leaf structure free of foliar lesions or defoliation
classes.organicTreatment: Maintain regular foliar compost tea and balanced organic nutrition.
classes.chemicalTreatment: None required.
classes.preventativeAction: Routine crop scouting and drip irrigation to maintain ideal root-zone moisture.

symptoms: Shot-hole perforations across foliage from flea beetles
Chewed leaf margins and wilting terminal shoots from shoot borers
classes.organicTreatment: Apply neem oil (0.5%) spray or pyrethrin-based botanical extract in early morning.
classes.chemicalTreatment: Rotate targeted insecticides (e.g., chlorantraniliprole or spinosad per label instructions).
classes.preventativeAction: Deploy yellow sticky traps and pheromone traps across the field perimeter.

symptoms: Circular to irregular chlorotic spots turning gray-brown
Concentric rings with darker margins on mature lower leaves
classes.organicTreatment: Copper hydroxide or copper octanoate protective spray; remove lower infected foliage.
classes.chemicalTreatment: Apply preventative mancozeb or difenoconazole at first lesion onset.
classes.preventativeAction: Promote wide row spacing for canopy airflow; avoid overhead sprinkler irrigation.

classes.scientificPathogen: Tobacco Mosaic Virus (TMV) / Cucumber Mosaic Virus (CMV)
symptoms: Interveinal mosaic mottling with alternating light and dark green patches
Leaf puckering, distortion, and stunted canopy growth
classes.organicTreatment: No curative treatment exists; rogue out and destroy severely infected plants immediately.
classes.chemicalTreatment: Control vector aphid and thrip populations using systemic insecticide.
classes.preventativeAction: Disinfect tools with 10% trisodium phosphate; sanitize hands between plants.

symptoms: Severe leaf miniaturization and shortened internodes
Excessive bushy shoots with phyllody (floral parts transformed into leaves)
classes.organicTreatment: Uproot and burn diseased plants; spray botanical neem repellent against leafhoppers.
classes.chemicalTreatment: Apply imidacloprid or dimethoate to suppress vector leafhopper populations.
classes.preventativeAction: Eradicate alternate weed hosts around the plot perimeter before planting.

symptoms: Cottony white mycelial fungal growth on leaves and stem base
Black irregular sclerotia bodies embedded within collapsing tissue
classes.organicTreatment: Soil drench with antagonistic Trichoderma harzianum; prune infected branches.
classes.chemicalTreatment: Apply preventative boscalid, cyprodinil, or iprodione during high humidity.
classes.preventativeAction: Practice 3-year non-host crop rotation; improve soil drainage and reduce plant density.

symptoms: Rapid daytime wilting without prominent initial leaf yellowing
Vascular browning and milky bacterial ooze when stem is placed in clear water
classes.organicTreatment: Incorporate bio-fumigant mustard cover crops; rogue out wilted specimens immediately.
classes.chemicalTreatment: No effective chemical curative; copper bactericides provide limited soil suppression.
classes.preventativeAction: Graft commercial varieties onto resistant rootstocks; maintain raised beds.

symptoms: Dark brown circular lesions with concentric target rings
Chlorotic yellow halo surrounding older foliage lesions
classes.organicTreatment: Apply copper octanoate spray; remove and destroy lower infected leaves.
classes.chemicalTreatment: Rotate preventative chlorothalonil or azoxystrobin fungicides per label intervals.
classes.preventativeAction: Utilize drip irrigation to avoid leaf wetness; mulch soil to halt spore splash.

symptoms: Large irregular water-soaked dark olive to purplish lesions
White downy mold sporulation visible on leaf undersides in humid mornings
classes.organicTreatment: Immediate foliar copper sulfate application; destroy heavily infected crops.
classes.chemicalTreatment: Apply systemic cymoxanil, mandipropamid, or metalaxyl upon first regional alert.
classes.preventativeAction: Scout aggressively during cool, foggy weather; destroy volunteer tomato cull piles.

symptoms: Numerous small circular spots with dark brown margins and gray centers
Tiny black pycnidia specks visible within lesion centers
classes.organicTreatment: Bio-fungicidal Bacillus subtilis spray; strip bottom 12 inches of foliage.
classes.chemicalTreatment: Apply chlorothalonil or mancozeb at 7 to 10 day intervals.
classes.preventativeAction: Avoid overhead watering; disinfect stakes and tomato cages between seasons.

symptoms: Severe upward leaf curling and cupping with interveinal yellowing
Severe plant stunting and flower abortion leading to minimal fruit set
classes.organicTreatment: No viral cure; rogue infected plants; spray insecticidal soap or neem against whiteflies.
classes.chemicalTreatment: Systemic neonicotinoids or cyantraniliprole targeting Bemisia tabaci vector.
classes.preventativeAction: Use insect-proof netting (50-mesh) on nurseries; use TYLCV-resistant hybrids.

symptoms: Pale green to yellow spots on upper leaf surface
Olive-green to brown velvety fungal growth on matching lower leaf surface
classes.organicTreatment: Foliar sulfur dust or potassium bicarbonate spray; prune inner canopy for airflow.
classes.chemicalTreatment: Apply preventative thiophanate-methyl or azoxystrobin fungicides.
classes.preventativeAction: Maintain relative humidity below 85% in greenhouse or polytunnel enclosures.

symptoms: Vibrant green leaves with firm turgor and normal serration
No necrosis, chlorosis, or pathogen sporulation
classes.organicTreatment: Standard balanced organic fish hydrolysate or kelp foliar feed.
classes.chemicalTreatment: None required.
classes.preventativeAction: Continue regular scouting and balanced nitrogen-potassium crop nutrition.

symptoms: Sunken circular necrotic lesions with concentric acervuli rings
Black fungal microsclerotia and premature leaf senescence
classes.organicTreatment: Neem oil foliar application; wettable sulfur in early morning hours.
classes.chemicalTreatment: Mancozeb or pyraclostrobin application during early canopy and fruit development.
classes.preventativeAction: Use certified pathogen-free seeds; practice 3-year Solanaceae crop rotation.

symptoms: Small dark water-soaked spots enlarging into circular brown lesions
Lesions blistered or scab-like with yellow chlorotic borders
classes.organicTreatment: Copper bactericide (copper hydroxide) combined with biological Bacillus subtilis.
classes.chemicalTreatment: Streptomycin sulfate tank-mix where locally registered for agricultural use.
classes.preventativeAction: Sanitize seed with hot-water treatment (50°C for 25 min); avoid handling wet plants.

symptoms: Circular lesions with light gray centers and prominent dark brown borders
Premature defoliation starting from the lower canopy during humid periods
classes.organicTreatment: Apply copper octanoate; remove fallen infected debris to lower inoculum.
classes.chemicalTreatment: Apply chlorothalonil or carbendazim preventative sprays at 10-day intervals.
classes.preventativeAction: Maintain adequate spacing; mulch beds with rice straw or plastic film.

symptoms: Upward curling, puckering, and crinkling of leaf blades
Severe vein thickening, bushiness, and stunted terminal growth
classes.organicTreatment: Rogue out symptomatic plants; spray mineral oil or neem to repel whiteflies and thrips.
classes.chemicalTreatment: Imidacloprid or diafenthiuron applied to suppress vector whitefly populations.
classes.preventativeAction: Install silver reflective mulches; cultivate maize or sorghum border trap crops.

symptoms: Interveinal chlorosis on young foliage (Fe) or generalized pale yellowing on older leaves (N)
Stunted vegetative expansion without distinct fungal or bacterial lesion borders
classes.organicTreatment: Apply chelated iron or balanced foliar seaweed and fish amino acid extract.
classes.chemicalTreatment: Foliar application of 19-19-19 water-soluble NPK fertilizer with micronutrients.
classes.preventativeAction: Conduct routine soil pH testing; maintain soil pH between 6.0 and 6.8.

symptoms: Small bleached chalk-white or off-white spots across leaf surface
Thinning leaf tissue susceptible to shot-hole tearing under wind
classes.organicTreatment: Protective copper fungicide spray; improve plant nutrition and vigor.
classes.chemicalTreatment: Difenoconazole or tebuconazole spray at early disease detection.
classes.preventativeAction: Avoid overhead water splash; ensure good air movement through pruning.

symptoms: Glossy uniform deep green leaf color
Firm leaf lamina without curling, lesions, or abiotic chlorosis
classes.organicTreatment: Routine foliar bio-stimulant or compost tea nourishment.
classes.chemicalTreatment: None required.
classes.preventativeAction: Maintain balanced moisture schedule and periodic canopy scouting.
